reuse.why: Most actions share the new category selector and reuse existing tag, spreadsheet, mutation, and undo helpers, but copyPreviousMonth retains independent eligibility logic.

duplication.why: The selector removes repeated category queries, but hidden/template eligibility remains duplicated in copyPreviousMonth and income eligibility remains repeated across actions.

placement.why: Category selection and budget calculations remain in server budget actions, with handler registration in the existing application layer.

scope.why: The edits are focused on the requested month-wide actions, their method registration, and associated tests.

maintainability.why: The shared selector improves ownership, but maintaining a separate eligibility implementation for copyPreviousMonth leaves the central policy vulnerable to further divergence.

bypasses_abstraction.where: packages/loot-core/src/server/budget/actions.ts: copyPreviousMonth bypasses getMonthWideBudgetCategories and applies its own hidden/template checks.

disguised_duplication.where: In actions.ts, copyPreviousMonth expresses hidden/template eligibility as imperative guards over getBudgetData results while getMonthWideBudgetCategories expresses the same policy through SQL predicates.

abstraction_drift.where: getMonthWideBudgetCategories gains the requested includeHiddenCategories parameter and SQL override branch, while copyPreviousMonth independently evolves its eligibility checks instead of using the shared selector.
